items.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016
items.q: I got a call from Chuck’s manager, a guy named Richard Burkhart asking me if I was interested.

ctx.x: Well I started working with Chuck in 2000. And like you, I mean before he broke nationally he was kind of a regional star here with the “Friends and Love” recording. And I loved his music. Never in my wildest dreams did I think that our paths would ever cross all these years later. But I had moved to Nashville in ‘97 because I wanted to check out the songwriting scene and Mike had moved to Nashville and our drummer George Perilli had moved there. And I kind of wanted to take a break from the L.A. treadmill that I…

was kind of indulging the songwriting thing, and I got a call from Chuck’s manager, a guy named Richard Burkhart asking me if I was interested. And apparently a guy that I knew in L.A., a bass player named Charles Meeks, who had played with Chuck forever, great Charles, lovely guy, great player, played on all the hits, “Feels So Good” and he decided to retire. And I knew Grant Geissman and I’d played with Grant quite a bit in L.A. He was Chuck’s guitar player, played the famous solo on “Feels So Good.” And so…
